text: In Genesis 22 a question is raised, and no answer is supplied. Abraham is commanded to take his son, his only son, whom he loves; yet of what he feels on receiving the command no account is given, nor does the narrator describe the inward life of Abraham. He offers no protest, and enters into no bargaining; of the man who had argued for Sodom there is here no sign. Abraham is set before us less as a character than as a silence, and that silence is the central point of the chapter.
